title: Loops
summary: Repeat work with for loops and while loops, use range(), and learn to spot and fix a loop that never ends.
objectives: Repeat an action a fixed number of times with for and range()
Repeat an action while a condition is True with a while loop
Recognise and fix an infinite loop

segments.title: What you will build
segments.body:
## What you will build

In this lab you add up the numbers 1 to 100 twice: once with a `for` loop and `range()`, and once with a `while` loop. Both loops must give the same answer, 5050, and your program prints both totals and whether they match. The `while` loop in the starter has a bug: its counter never goes up, so the loop never ends. You will see what a real infinite loop looks like, then fix it by adding one line. By the end you will know when to reach for `for` and when to reach for `while`.

lab.title: Sum 1 to 100 two ways
lab.objective: Add the numbers 1 to 100 with a for loop and with a while loop, fix the infinite loop, and show both totals agree.
lab.instructions:
Two loops, one job: add up every whole number from 1 to 100.

1. Finish the for loop. It uses range(1, 101) to visit each number n; inside the loop add n to for_total.
2. Fix the while loop. Right now count never changes, so the loop never ends. If you press Run before fixing it, your program is stopped after a few seconds for taking too long: that is an infinite loop. Add a line inside the loop that increases count by 1 each time round.
3. Print three lines, exactly like this:

For loop total: 5050
While loop total: 5050
Same answer: True

The third line prints the comparison for_total == while_total.
lab.constraints: Keep the variable names for_total, while_total and count. Keep count = 1 and while count <= 100: as given. Do not type 5050 yourself; let the loops work it out. Do not use input().
lab.starter_code:
# Part 1: the for loop version
for_total = 0
for n in range(1, 101):
    # 1. Add n to for_total
    pass

# Part 2: the while loop version
# 2. This loop never ends because count never changes. Fix it!
while_total = 0
count = 1
while count <= 100:
    while_total = while_total + count

# 3. Print the three lines (see the instructions)
hints: Inside the for loop, replace pass with for_total = for_total + n. In the while loop, ask yourself: what has to change so that count <= 100 eventually becomes False?
A while loop only ends when its condition becomes False. Add count = count + 1 as the last line inside the while loop, indented like the line above it.
After both loops: print("For loop total:", for_total), print("While loop total:", while_total) and print("Same answer:", for_total == while_total).

visible_examples.description: Adding 1 to 5 with a for loop
visible_examples.code:
total = 0
for n in range(1, 6):
    total = total + n
print("Total:", total)

visible_examples.description: A while loop that counts to 3 (note the line that changes count)
visible_examples.code:
count = 1
while count <= 3:
    print("count is", count)
    count = count + 1
print("Done")
visible_examples.expected_output:
count is 1
count is 2
count is 3
Done

success_criteria: while_total is 5050 (so the while loop ends)
Your program prints Same answer: True
The three lines are printed exactly as shown
The while loop's counter finishes at 101

tests.label: for_total is 5050
tests.remediation: Inside the for loop, replace pass with for_total = for_total + n so every number from 1 to 100 is added.

tests.label: while_total is 5050 (the while loop ends)
tests.remediation: Add count = count + 1 as the last line inside the while loop so the loop ends, and keep adding count to while_total before that line.
tests.objective: Repeat with while and fix an infinite loop

tests.label: Your program prints Same answer: True
tests.remediation: Add print("Same answer:", for_total == while_total) after both loops. It prints True only when both totals match.

definition.description: Your program prints Same answer: True

tests.label: The three lines are printed exactly as shown
tests.remediation: Print exactly three lines: For loop total: 5050, While loop total: 5050 and Same answer: True. Check spelling, capital letters and the colons.

tests.label: The while loop's counter finishes at 101
tests.remediation: Keep count = 1 and while count <= 100: as given, and increase count by exactly 1 each time round. When the loop ends, count is 101.
tests.objective: Repeat with while and fix an infinite loop

lab.solution:
for_total = 0
for n in range(1, 101):
    for_total = for_total + n

while_total = 0
count = 1
while count <= 100:
    while_total = while_total + count
    count = count + 1

print("For loop total:", for_total)
print("While loop total:", while_total)
print("Same answer:", for_total == while_total)
